[ASSISTANT_SAID] Ukuleles are amazing instruments.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The main differences between soprano, concert, and tenor ukuleles lie in their size, scale length, and tone.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Soprano Ukulele: Smallest of the three, body length around 20 inches, scale length 13-14 inches, bright and punchy tone, suitable for beginners.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Concert Ukulele: Slightly larger, body length around 23-24 inches, scale length 15-16 inches, warmer and fuller tone, popular choice for beginners and intermediate players.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tenor Ukulele: Largest of the three, body length around 26-27 inches, scale length 17-18 inches, deeper and richer tone, preferred by more experienced players.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] When choosing between these three, consider hand size, playing style, desired sound, and budget.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested resources for learning ukulele chords and fingerpicking patterns include Ukulele Tricks, Uke Lessons, The Ukulele Teacher, Ukulele Buddy, and Fender Play.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested fingerpicking resources include Ukulele Fingerpicking Patterns and Fingerstyle Ukulele YouTube channel.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] As a guitar player, user will find that many skills transfer nicely to the ukulele, including chord shapes, finger independence, hand positioning, and strumming techniques.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] User should focus on developing ukulele-specific skills while also rebuilding calluses from guitar playing.  
[USER] User is considering whether to focus on building up calluses again before learning ukulele or to dive right in.
